title: Transitions in cognitive capacity are gradual, not binary

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Transitions in cognitive capacity are gradual, not binary

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Although major differences in cognitive function exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents; cognition-related properties form a continuum from humble proto-cognitive systems to advanced minds.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Specifically, while major differences in cognitive function of course exist among diverse intelligences, transitions between them have not been shown to be binary or rapid relative to the timescale of individual agents.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: A Proposal for a Framework › Philosophical Foundations of an Approach to Diverse Intelligences”. Scope: All cognitive systems across evolution, development and bioengineered hybrids

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Selected capacities and transitions can be analyzed quantitatively, but no existing dataset spans the claim's enormous scope. Different operationalizations can yield continuous or discontinuous patterns.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Choose comparable cognitive capacities, quantify them across phylogenetic, developmental, and engineered transitions, and test whether their distributions show discontinuities larger and faster than prespecified thresholds relative to agent timescales.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available datasets cover a highly biased subset of systems.

Binary and rapid require arbitrary thresholds.

Cognition lacks a single cross-system scale.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.35
data adequacy: 0.22
data existence: 0.52
discriminating power: 0.35
operationalizability: 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative compilations of brain size, neuron number, and learning scores exist as scattered published tables and can be tested for saltations versus grades on those proxies. No single public matrix covers cognition across the claim's full range of organisms, and competing proxies answer differently. The result can pressure a strong binary reading and cannot settle cognitive capacity as such.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: On one pre-registered cognitive or neural trait, test whether sister lineages differ by jumps that are large relative to within-lineage variation and short relative to individual lifespan; a continuum holds if changes are graded on that trait.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Have not been shown' is a claim about the literature as well as about the organisms.

A graded proxy can hide a qualitative change in a capacity the proxy does not measure.

Neuron counts, brain size, and learning scores are different operationalizations and need not agree.
